title: Dolphins in Florida Build a Net Out of Mud, and the Fish Jump In

scenes.text: Florida dolphins catch fish with a net made of mud.
In the shallows of Florida Bay, one bottlenose dolphin swims a tight circle around a school of fish, beating its tail on the bottom.
A ring of mud rises and closes in. The fish won't swim through the cloud.
So they jump over it. The rest of the pod is waiting outside the ring with their mouths open.
It has been seen almost only among bottlenose dolphins in a few parts of Florida. One calf was watched learning it from its mother.
And one dolphin was filmed doing it alone: build the wall, then race around to catch its own fish. It worked about one time in three.

description:
Bottlenose dolphins in a few parts of Florida hunt by 'mud-ring feeding': one dolphin circles a school of fish while beating its tail on the shallow bottom, raising a ring of mud.
The fish, probably mullet, avoid the muddy water and leap over the ring, often straight into the mouths of the waiting dolphins. A solo dolphin filmed near St. Petersburg managed it alone about a third of the time, and an observer has seen a young dolphin learning the technique from its mother.
Which animal has the smartest hunting trick?

first_comment: The first big study of mud-ring feeding came out in 2005. Which animal should we cover next: the smartest hunter or the laziest?
